feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.095 m, kp 3.5, kd 0.6) scored 327.8, the best so far, with oval finish 0.75 and s-bend max_error 0.0615 m, while s-bend finish stayed at 0 in all 20 trials. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m) gave s-bend max_error 0.0645 m with s-bend oscillation 0.27, and iteration 2 (wheel_track 0.10 m) gave oscillation 0.43 on the s-bend. That pattern suggests the s-bend failure is overshoot, not jitter. Sensing is not the binding limit: iteration 1's wider row cut line loss but lost completions. In the controller I kept kp 3.5, kd 0.6, ki 0.2 and base_speed 1.4 unchanged, so this race isolates the sensor forward offset. Read the next race as follows. If s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m and the oval finish holds at or above 0.5, keep y = 0.06 m as the lookahead lever. If s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.43 with no fall in line loss, the extra lookahead is adding jitter, so an intermediate forward offset of y = 0.05 m is the next test. If the oval finish drops to 0.45 or below with no s-bend gain, return the row to y = 0.04 m.
requested_changes: Move the sensor row forward from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.06 m, keeping five sensors at x = ±0.04 m with 0.02 m spacing and 12 mm footprints. Evidence: iteration 4 left s-bend max_error at 0.0615 m with zero s-bend finishes, so more lookahead is the next lever.

If the s-bend finish stays at 0 and max_error stays near 0.0615 m, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.05 m with the same five-sensor count, keeping y at the chosen forward offset. Evidence: iteration 0 lost the tape at about ±0.058 m, and iteration 1 cut s-bend line loss from 1.1 to 0.2 when coverage was widened.

If the oval finish falls to 0.45 or below with no s-bend gain, return the row to y = 0.04 m and keep wheel_track at 0.095 m. Evidence: iteration 4 gave an oval finish of 0.75, while iteration 2 at 0.10 m gave 0.45 and iteration 0 at 0.12 m gave 0.05.
